newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 8.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Hindustan Times
CRISIS IN RAJASTHAN GOVERNMENT DEEPENS

The crisis in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Rajasthan deepened with three more legislators demanding the ouster of the chief minister. The legislators also threatened to form a separate group in the assembly if the party's central leadership failed to remove him. Although the BJP leadership claimed the dissent was not serious, the chief minister is rushing back from a foreign trip to discuss the crisis with senior party leaders. The BJP, keeping in mind the Gujarat episode where a revolt split their ranks and brought down the government, was not going to take any chances in Rajasthan where it has a slim majority.
Indian Express
INDIA WINS AT WORLD TRADE ORGANISATION

India scored a victory over the United States after a trade panel rejected U.S. claims that textile exports from India were destabilising its domestic markets. A World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel, formed at India's behest, concluded that the U.S. restraints applied since April 1995 on imports of woven wool shirts and blouses from India and its extensions violated the provisions of the Agreement on Textiles and Clothings. The panel ruled there was no evidence that increased imports of Indian woollen shirts into the United States had damaged the U.S. industry, officials said.
The Economic Times
OIL MAJORS TO TARGET BOND MARKET

The spiralling oil pool deficit has forced two oil majors to tap the bond market to bridge their working capital requirements. While Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) is planning a one billion rupee issue, with a greenshoe option of the same amount, Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) is looking at a 2-2.5 billion rupee issue. BPCL is yet to decide the greenshoe option. HPCL is going in for a one-year maturity paper, while BPCL's paper will have a three-year tenure.
AMERICAN INTERNATIONAL GROUP BUYS 13 PCT IN CIBA CKD

American International Group (AIG) is investing, through its subsidiary Keenan Ltd, 161.2 million rupees in Ciba CKD Biochem Ltd, a joint venture between Ciba Geigy and Chong Kun Dang of Korea. The placement, organised by UTI Exchange Securities Ltd, would give AIG a 13 percent stake in Ciba CKD. The $1.06 billion AIG infrastructure fund has investments in India including in Modicom, Tata Bell Canada and Ballabgarh Power. AIG, along with the Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services Ltd, is now in the process of finalising the AIG Indian Sectoral Equity Fund to target investments in the infrastructure sector in India.
INTERCONNECT CHARGES CLIPPED BY 40 PCT

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) caved in to a longstanding demand of the basic service operators by clipping the interconnection charges by about 40 percent. Communications Minister Beni Prasad Verma said the interconnect charges for a 2-megabit link had been reduced from 96,000 rupees to 54,000 rupees per year. Verma said the DoT's move reflected the government's commitment to liberalisation and expressed hope that basic service operators would not shrink from paying the licence fee.
Financial Express
INDUSTRY, CIVIL AVIATION MINISTRIES ON COLLISION COURSE

The approval of the proposed 24.8 billion rupee domestic airline venture of Tata-Singapore Airlines (Tata-SIA) has put the Industry Ministry on a collision course with the Civil Aviation Ministry. The civil aviation minister is upset with the Foreign Investment Promotion Board's decision as it opposed his stand that foreign airlines would not be allowed to hold equity stake in domestic airlines. The decision has taken political overtones with one of the constituents of the coalition government questioning the decision.
MINIMUM ALTERNATE TAX MAY CHECK BANKS' GAINS

Many state-owned banks will not avail of the depreciation write-back benefit on their investments even though yields of government securities in the secondary market in 1996/97 have declined. If the banks use this facility to boost both book profit and their reserves, they would be subject to the minimum alternate tax. Instead, profit-making banks are planning to use the depreciation benefit to push the quantum of current investments beyond the central bank stipulation.
Business Standard
RESERVE BANK PLANS TO GRANT BANKS GREATER FREEDOM

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is planning to grant more autonomy to the public sector banks on a selective basis. The RBI is expected to allow more freedom in the area of branch expansion. The RBI's decision on the issue is expected to come through by the end of the month. Bankers are eagerly looking forward to a favourable decision from the RBI as this would give them more operational freedom.
ALTERNATIVE MODES FOR SELLOFF PROPOSED

The Disinvestment Commission is exploring alternative modes of disinvestment of government stake in public sector units (PSUs). So far, the government has only explored the offer for sales route as a means of disinvestment. Among the modalities outlined for disinvestment is the strategic sale of majority stake with management control in select PSUs. Alternatively, the sale of minority stake, supplemented by technology transfer arrangements, can also be considered. For PSUs with a strong asset base, the commission has proposed leasing of government assets to the highest bidder.
IMPORT CURBS TO BE LIFTED BY 2001

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs would discuss a proposal on Wednesday that seeks to commit India to a five-stage phase-out of its licensing restrictions on select items of imports including consumer durables by 2001. The commitment would be at the core of India's negotiating stand at the forthcoming round of discussion with the International Monetary Fund and the World Trade Organisation on January 18 in Geneva. Official sources said the time schedule was decided after taking into consideration the expected foreign exchange outgo that the removal of these restrictions would entail.
The Observer
FINANCE MINISTRY VETOES PUBLIC ISSUE THIS FISCAL

The Finance Ministry has asked Canara Bank, Bank of India and Corporation Bank to defer their public issues to fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). The public issues of these banks were earlier slated for January-February 1997. The ministry's ruling came in the wake of its decision of not allowing the nationalised banks to tap stock market this year. Banking sources said the decision had been taken by the Finance Ministry keeping in mind the present sluggishness in the capital market.
MARUTI FAMILY SILVER NOT TO BE SOLD OFF TO SUZUKI

The Industry Ministry has decided to maintain the status quo as regards the ownership of Maruti Udyog Ltd (MUL). Accordingly, the present 50:50 equity holding in MUL between the government and Suzuki Motor Corporation (SMC) would continue. The ministry's decision came as a setback to SMC's efforts to get a controlling stake in MUL. SMC had recently made an open offer to buy out 24 percent of the government stake in MUL in a bid to increase its stake 74 percent. SMC had argued this was necessary in order to face growing competition from a large number of multinational companies.
